notes.title: Women’s Day Steam Sale 2025
notes.content:

notes.title: Montreal Comiccon - Le Zone de Jeu Indie
notes.content:
Every year,  Le Zone de Jeux Indie Loto-Quebec invites a selection of games to showcase on the expo floor of Montreal Comiccon…. and this year they chose Shards Between Us! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44798971/d1bf2e05896884194229c6b30585f8a4f62fab92.jpg[/img]

Arka, Nora, and Elisabeth reunited (in-person for the first time since GDC!) and had a lovely time catching up while sharing our little plant-puzzler. With Comiccon attracting 65,000 of our closest friends, we spent three fan-packed days showcasing our demo, chatting with fellow developers, and admiring all the AMAZING costumes of attendees. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44798971/f768d3a4b9c9efca46ce7b595c6cc9c521358075.jpg[/img]

Take a look yourself in this amazing interview of Nora IN FRENCH -  live on Loto Quebec’s Twitch channel:

https://www.twitch.tv/videos/2194924061?collection=6WU9DSRy3xd5Qg

They even chose us for a live stream where they played our demo <3

https://www.twitch.tv/videos/2191830802?collection=6WU9DSRy3xd5Qg&t=1h29m54s

Thank you so much to everyone who’s helped us along our journey so far and to everyone that stopped by the booth to play our demo at Montreal Comiccon! 

We couldn’t have made it this far without you.

- Elisabeth

notes.title: Develop Conference 2024
notes.content:
Queensguard’s resident Animator and Artist, Charlotte, had the pleasure of attending [url=https://www.developconference.com/]Develop Brighton[/url] this year! Weather wise it was a mixed bag, but as an event it was a great time as always. 

This year, Queensguard showcased Shards Between Us at #RaiseTheGame’s Festival of Food Evening sponsored by UsTwo and Jagex. It was a real honour to be showcasing with the Code Coven booth where we represented Code Coven Alumni! The evening was amazing with so much delicious food! Pizza, Rice Bowls and Ice Cream Sandwiches all night… a Game Developer’s dream. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44798971/68f7a43b9c21f4c1666846ca73384ba93df4e81f.jpg[/img]

After many fantastic meetups on the beachfront, including a quick dip in the sea with the good sunshine, we had a table at the Brilliant Indie Treasures Showcase! Taking place in a bank after closing hours it was a surreal backdrop but incredibly wholesome experience. It was fantastic to see so many familiar faces also exhibiting there.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44798971/d6d24454b63e2fd93d3cf88b33e20c051792e591.jpg[/img]

A huge thank you to the Brilliant Indie Treasures team for organising such a wonderful event! I was really grateful to have such wonderful showcase neighbors too with Lost In Cult and Draknek & Friends either side. It was great to feel a strong sense of community especially with the tough times in the industry right now. 

Thank you so much to everyone who gave our little Plant Puzzle Game a try! It was a pleasure to represent Queensguard at Develop:Brighton Events. 

- Charlotte

notes.title: ThinkyCon
notes.content:
[url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/liney-io/]Caroline Clark[/url], our Game Director and Programmer, spoke at [url=https://thinkygames.com/thinkycon/]ThinkyCon 2024[/url] about her top tips for programming indie thinky games. 

"[i]Good coding means maximising my available working memory. 
Automated testing helped me build the ivy feature in Shards Between Us.[/i]" - Caroline Clark

[h2]Tips to make programming your game less hellish[/h2]
Making games in small teams or solo is more possible than it’s ever been, and you can see this in the explosion of indie games and game jams. Yet you might find that, as you take your three-day caffeine powered game jam project to being a fully fledged masterpiece, you have a sinking feeling that you're building it “wrong”, but you can’t figure out why or what to do about it. 

Caroline talks about the time sinks she's found in coding, give examples for common pitfalls and offers practical tips to help you make your indie games.
